name: Coombs Indirect
description: The Indirect Coombs Test (Indirect Antiglobulin Test - IAT) detects antibodies in the patient's serum or plasma that can bind to red blood cells. It is used for antibody screening, crossmatching before blood transfusion, and investigating hemolytic anemias.
literatureReview: The Indirect Coombs Test (IAT) is a laboratory procedure used to detect antibodies in a patient's serum that are capable of binding to red blood cells. It is routinely performed for pre-transfusion compatibility testing, antibody screening, and investigation of hemolytic anemias. The test involves incubating patient serum with reagent red cells, followed by the addition of anti-human globulin reagent. A positive result indicates the presence of clinically significant red cell antibodies.
